items.claim: average() divides by len(prices) with no empty-list guard, so it raises ZeroDivisionError on an empty cart, which the PR body and docstring both say is a common case.
items.consequence: A new cart has no items, so the summary panel calls average([]); total([]) returns 0, then 0 / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError and the panel fails to render instead of showing 0.0 or 'no items'.

items.claim: The docstring says empty lists are common and implies they're handled, but the code doesn't handle them and the function doesn't say what it returns for an empty cart.
items.consequence: A caller reads 'empty lists are common for new carts', assumes average([]) is safe, and skips its own guard; the summary panel then crashes on every new cart.

items.claim: No tests were added for average(), neither for the normal case nor for the empty-cart case the PR says it supports.
items.consequence: A test like average([]) would have caught the ZeroDivisionError before merge; without one, the empty-cart crash only shows up in the summary panel in production.
